newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - IPE Brent's "inside day" quiets bulls.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - IPE Brent's "inside day" quiets bulls.

text.p: IPE November Brent and gas oil may be in for another session of sideways to slightly lower prices as the market takes a breather after scorching rallies to post-Gulf War highs this week, some technical analysts said.
But any correction would likely find quick and solid support, particularly for Nov Brent at $24.00 and then $23.60-$23.63 where previous highs now serve as support.
Nov Brent posted an "inside trading day" on Wednesday by staying within its previous session range, which would normally suggest a pause or consolidation in the larger uptrend.

The nine- and 14-day RSIs on both Nov Brent and gas oil may be turning lower after prices peaked earlier this week, chartists said, even though Brent's momentum levels are below the peaks reached when prices rallied last month.
"I don't think the RSIs look too overbought," with the nine-day at 68 percent on crude, said Adrian Haylor, technical analyst at Sucden in London.

"It looks as though it could have some sort of correction but that correction should hold at $23.60," he said. "Anything around $24 and above $23.60 would be an opportunity to enter the market (to buy)...Clearly the bull market remains intact."
Further support is at Nov Brent's 20-day moving average near $23.10 and 40-day moving average near $22, Haylor said.
Nov Brent is expected to open 10 to 15 cents lower from its settlement on Wednesday at $24.27.

Nov gas oil, which becomes the spot month today, fell $3.75 to $234.50 at 0822 GMT. The contract rallied almost vertically from its September 20 low of $206.75 to its contract high of $243.25 on Tuesday.
The expiry of the Oct contract, which is trading $4.25 lower at $241.75, is likely to leave a gap on the continuation chart.
"Again, the longer-term trend is intact but in the short term it probably needs to go lower," Haylor said.
He said Nov gas oil could fall to as low as $220, near the 20-day moving average and just above the high of $217.50 hit when Brent rallied last month to their peak.
The nine- and 14-day RSIs were above 80 percent at Tuesday's price high and this morning had already fallen and were below 70 percent.
